column5: The police quickly arrived at the scene.
column6: 现场 is the place where something happens: 事故现场 (the scene of an accident), 现场表演 (a live show), 到现场 (to arrive on the spot).

column4: 这是一座很现代的城市。
column5: This is a very modern city.
column6: 现代 is modern, or the modern age: 现代人 (modern people), 现代音乐 (modern music), 现代化 (modernisation).

column5: This country is modernising.
column6: 现代化 is to make something modern, or modernisation: 实现现代化 (to achieve modernisation), 现代化的城市 (a modern city).

column5: This subway line is very convenient.
column6: 线路 is a line or a route for transport, electricity or a tour: 地铁线路 (a subway line), 旅行线路 (a travel route), 线路问题 (a wiring problem).

column5: Reality is different from imagination.
column6: 现实 is reality, or realistic: 面对现实 (to face reality), 现实生活 (real life), 很现实 (very realistic).

column5: This is a common phenomenon.
column6: 现象 is a phenomenon: 社会现象 (a social phenomenon), 常见的现象 (a common phenomenon).

column5: The school limits students from playing with their phones.
column6: 限制 is to limit, or a limit: 限制时间 (to limit time), 年龄限制 (an age limit).

column5: He is not satisfied with the present situation.
column6: 现状 is the situation as it is now: 了解现状 (to understand the present situation), 改变现状 (to change the situation).

column4: 这个乡很小，只有一所学校。
column5: This township is very small, with only one school.
column6: 乡 is a rural township, a unit smaller than a 县: 乡里 (in the township), 县和乡 (counties and townships). It is also in 家乡 and 乡村.

column5: He gets along very well with his classmates.
column6: 相处 is to get along with each other: 相处得很好 (to get along very well), 和他相处 (to get along with him).

column5: I like life in the countryside.
column6: 乡村 is the countryside, as opposed to the city: 乡村生活 (country life), 乡村学校 (a village school).

column5: This question is quite difficult.
column6: 相当 is "quite, rather" before an adjective: 相当好 (rather good), 相当大 (quite big). It can also mean "equal to", but the adverb use is the common one.

column4: 这家店的东西相对便宜。
column5: The things in this shop are relatively cheap.
column6: 相对 is relative, or to face each other: 相对来说 (relatively speaking), 相对便宜 (relatively cheap), 相对而坐 (to sit facing each other).

column5: This matter is related to him.
column6: 相关 is related: 相关的人 (the people involved), 和…相关 (related to …). The opposite is 无关.

column4: 他们两个人的样子很相似。
column5: The two of them look very similar.
column6: 相似 is similar: 很相似 (very similar), 相似的地方 (similar points).

column5: I miss my family very much.
column6: 想念 is to miss someone or something far away: 想念家人 (to miss one's family), 想念家乡 (to miss one's hometown).

column4: 半夜里，我听到了一个响声。
column5: In the middle of the night, I heard a noise.
column6: 响声 is a sound or noise that something makes: 很大的响声 (a loud noise), 没有响声 (no sound).

column4: 我喜欢享受安静的生活。
column5: I like to enjoy a quiet life.
column6: 享受 is to enjoy something good: 享受生活 (to enjoy life), 享受阳光 (to enjoy the sunshine).

column4: 你能想象这里以前的样子吗？
column5: Can you imagine how this place used to look?
column6: 想象 is to imagine, or imagination: 想象一下 (just imagine), 比想象的好 (better than imagined).

column4: 这本相册里有很多老照片。
column5: This photo album has many old photos.
column6: 相册 is a photo album: 一本相册 (a photo album), 看相册 (to look at an album).

column5: This project needs three months.
column6: 项目 is a project or an item on a list: 新项目 (a new project), 运动项目 (a sports event).

column5: My eraser has gone missing.
column6: 橡皮 is an eraser: 一块橡皮 (an eraser), 用橡皮 (to use an eraser).

column5: Please look up.
column6: 向上 is "upward": 向上看 (to look up), 向上走 (to go up), 积极向上 (positive and aspiring).

column5: Red stands for joy in China.
column6: 象征 is to stand for something, or a symbol: 象征和平 (to symbolise peace), 一个象征 (a symbol).

column4: 现在的年轻人喜欢在网上消费。
column5: Young people now like to spend money online.
column6: 消费 is to spend money on goods and services: 消费水平 (the spending level), 在网上消费 (to spend online).

column4: 消费者都喜欢便宜的东西。
column5: Consumers all like cheap things.
column6: 消费者 is a consumer: 消费者的意见 (consumers' opinions), 一位消费者 (a consumer). The ending 者 means "a person who does something".

column5: If one eats too fast, it is not easy to digest.
column6: 消化 is to digest food, or to take in knowledge: 消化食物 (to digest food), 消化知识 (to take in knowledge).

column5: He is very negative about his work.
column6: 消极 is negative or passive in attitude: 消极的想法 (negative thoughts), 态度消极 (a negative attitude). The opposite is 积极.

column5: The sales of this phone are very high.
column6: 销量 is the quantity sold: 销量高 (high sales), 提高销量 (to raise sales).

column4: 太阳出来以后，雾慢慢消失了。
column5: After the sun came out, the fog slowly disappeared.
column6: 消失 is to disappear gradually: 慢慢消失 (to vanish slowly), 消失了 (has disappeared). 不见了 is the everyday way to say something is gone.

column5: This company sells computers.
column6: 销售 is to sell, often by a company: 销售电脑 (to sell computers), 做销售 (to work in sales).

column5: Is Miss Zhang in?
column6: 小姐 is "Miss": 张小姐 (Miss Zhang), 这位小姐 (this young lady). Use it with care: in some places 小姐 can sound impolite, and 女士 is the safer polite word.

column5: This is a small car.
column6: 小型 is small-sized, as a type: 小型汽车 (a small car), 小型公司 (a small company). The opposite is 大型.

column5: Three is less than five.
column6: 小于 is "less than" in maths and rules: 三小于五 (three is less than five), 小于十岁 (under ten years old). The opposite is 大于.

column5: His efficiency at work is very high.
column6: 效率 is efficiency: 效率高 (high efficiency), 提高效率 (to raise efficiency).

column5: The photo on the wall is a little slanted.
column6: 斜 is slanted, not straight: 有点斜 (a little slanted), 斜了 (has become slanted).

column4: 两家公司签了一个协议。
column5: The two companies signed an agreement.
column6: 协议 is a formal agreement: 签协议 (to sign an agreement), 达成协议 (to reach an agreement).

column5: He likes writing.
column6: 写作 is writing as an activity or a skill: 写作课 (a writing class), 喜欢写作 (to like writing). 写 alone is the plain verb "to write".

column4: 新郎今天穿了一套黑西装。
column5: The groom wore a black suit today.
column6: 新郎 is the groom: 新郎新娘 (the bride and groom).

column5: A child's mental state is very important.
column6: 心理 is the mind, or a mental state: 心理问题 (a psychological problem), 心理准备 (mental preparation).

column5: The bride is very beautiful today.
column6: 新娘 is the bride: 新娘的衣服 (the bride's clothes), 新郎新娘 (the bride and groom).

column5: Everyone wishes this couple of newlyweds happiness.
column6: 新人 is a newly married person, or a newcomer at work: 一对新人 (a pair of newlyweds), 公司的新人 (a new person at a company).

column5: I really admire your idea.
column6: 欣赏 is to enjoy something beautiful, or to appreciate a person: 欣赏风景 (to enjoy the scenery), 欣赏他 (to admire him).

column5: A good mindset is very important.
column6: 心态 is one's state of mind: 好心态 (a good mindset), 心态不好 (a poor attitude).

column5: This is a new type of phone.
column6: 新型 is "of a new type": 新型手机 (a new-type phone), 新型汽车 (a new-type car).

column5: Please put the letter into the envelope.
column6: 信封 is an envelope: 一个信封 (an envelope), 信封上 (on the envelope).

column5: I trust my friend a lot.
column6: 信任 is to trust: 信任他 (to trust him), 得到信任 (to win trust).

column5: He keeps his word and never cheats people.
column6: 信用 is the trust earned by keeping one's word, or credit: 讲信用 (to keep one's word), 信用好 (good credit).

column5: The itinerary of this trip is very full.
column6: 行程 is a travel plan, or the distance travelled: 行程很满 (a packed schedule), 改行程 (to change the plan).

column5: Good habits are formed slowly.
column6: 形成 is to come into being: 形成习惯 (to form a habit), 形成想法 (to form an idea).

column5: We must act at once.
column6: 行动 is to take action, or an action: 马上行动 (to act at once), 行动起来 (to get into action).

column5: There are many pedestrians on the road.
column6: 行人 is a person walking on the road: 路上的行人 (pedestrians on the road), 让行人 (to give way to pedestrians).

column4: 你能形容一下那个人吗？
column5: Can you describe that person?
column6: 形容 is to describe how something looks or feels: 形容一下 (to describe a little), 无法形容 (impossible to describe).

column4: 这个活动的形式很特别。
column5: The form of this event is very special.
column6: 形式 is the form or way something takes: 不同的形式 (different forms), 形式和内容 (form and content).

column4: 现在的形势对我们很好。
column5: The present situation is very good for us.
column6: 形势 is the situation as it develops, often a big one: 国际形势 (the international situation), 形势很好 (the situation is good). 情况 is the plain word for "situation".

column4: 这辆车正在高速公路上行驶。
column5: This car is travelling on the motorway.
column6: 行驶 is for vehicles moving along a road: 在路上行驶 (to travel on the road), 慢慢行驶 (to drive slowly).

column5: His behaviour is very good.
column6: 行为 is behaviour or conduct: 好行为 (good behaviour), 坏行为 (bad behaviour).

column4: 老师在学生心里的形象很好。
column5: The teacher has a very good image in the students' hearts.
column6: 形象 is an image or a person's public look, or vivid: 好形象 (a good image), 很形象 (very vivid).

column4: 这块石头的形状很特别。
column5: The shape of this stone is very special.
column6: 形状 is shape: 圆的形状 (a round shape), 形状特别 (a special shape).

column4: 他受伤了，行走很不方便。
column5: He is injured, and walking is not very convenient.
column6: 行走 is to walk, more formal than 走: 行走不便 (walking is hard), 在路上行走 (to walk on the road).

column4: 我今天很幸运，买到了最后一张票。
column5: I am very lucky today; I bought the last ticket.
column6: 幸运 is lucky: 很幸运 (very lucky), 幸运的人 (a lucky person).

column4: 这两件事的性质不一样。
column5: The nature of these two matters is different.
column6: 性质 is the basic nature of something: 事情的性质 (the nature of a matter), 性质不同 (different in nature).

column4: 请再修改一下这篇文章。
column5: Please revise this article once more.
column6: 修改 is to change something to make it better: 修改文章 (to revise an article), 修改计划 (to change a plan).

column4: 政府要在这里修建一座桥。
column5: The government will build a bridge here.
column6: 修建 is to build big things such as roads and bridges: 修建公路 (to build a road), 修建桥 (to build a bridge).

column5: At weekends I like to relax at home.
column6: 休闲 is to relax, or leisure: 休闲生活 (leisure life), 休闲时间 (free time).

column5: Getting this done needs three days.
column6: 需 is a formal "need": 需要 is the usual word, while 需 appears in short phrases: 需三天 (needs three days), 需带 (must bring).

column4: 市场对这种手机的需求很大。
column5: The market demand for this kind of phone is very large.
column6: 需求 is a demand or a need: 市场需求 (market demand), 满足需求 (to meet a need).

column4: 他很虚心，愿意听别人的意见。
column5: He is modest and willing to listen to others' opinions.
column6: 虚心 is modest and willing to learn: 很虚心 (very modest), 虚心学习 (to learn with an open mind).

column5: The teacher announces that there is no class tomorrow.
column6: 宣布 is to announce officially: 宣布消息 (to announce news), 宣布结果 (to announce a result).

column4: 公司在电视上宣传新产品。
column5: The company is publicising a new product on TV.
column6: 宣传 is to make something widely known: 宣传活动 (to promote an event), 做宣传 (to do publicity).

column5: This contestant runs very fast.
column6: 选手 is a contestant in a competition: 参赛选手 (a contestant), 一名选手 (a contestant).

column5: This course has three credits.
column6: 学分 is a credit in school: 三个学分 (three credits), 拿学分 (to earn credits).

column4: 数学是我最喜欢的学科。
column5: Maths is my favourite subject.
column6: 学科 is a field of study: 数学学科 (the subject of maths), 不同学科 (different subjects).

column4: 这个工作要求大学学历。
column5: This job requires a university degree.
column6: 学历 is the highest level of school completed: 大学学历 (a university degree), 学历高 (a high level of education).

column5: The new school year starts in September.
column6: 学年 is a school year: 新学年 (the new school year), 一个学年 (a school year). A term is 学期.

column5: He is very interested in academic work.
column6: 学术 is academic study and research: 学术会议 (an academic conference), 学术研究 (academic research).
